{
  "summary": "Implement triage.sh to group noisy logs into stable error signatures by extracting the error message pattern (excluding variable parts like IDs), counting occurrences, and sorting by count descending. The script filters out non-error logs (INFO/WARN), extracts the signature by removing variable tokens, groups them, and outputs in the format 'COUNT SIGNATURE'.",
  "files": [
    {
      "path": "scripts/triage.sh",
      "content": "#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

LOG_FILE="${1:-}"

if [[ -z "$LOG_FILE" || ! -f "$LOG_FILE" ]]; then
    echo "Usage: $0 <log_file>" >&2
    exit 1
fi

# Process log file:
# 1. Filter only ERROR lines
# 2. Extract the message part (after the service name)
# 3. Normalize variable parts (orderId=..., sku=..., providerTxnId=..., email=...) to a placeholder
# 4. Count occurrences of each signature
# 5. Sort by count descending
# 6. Output: "COUNT SIGNATURE"

awk '
    /^ERROR/ {
        # Extract everything after the service name (second field)
        msg = ""
        for (i = 3; i <= NF; i++) {
            if (msg != "") msg = msg " "
            msg = msg $i
        }
        
        # Normalize variable patterns to a placeholder
        gsub(/orderId=[0-9]+/, "ID", msg)
        gsub(/sku=[a-zA-Z0-9]+/, "SKU", msg)
        gsub(/providerTxnId=[A-Z0-9]+/, "TXN", msg)
        gsub(/email=[a-zA-Z0-9.@]+/, "EMAIL", msg)
        
        signatures[msg]++
    }
    END {
        for (sig in signatures) {
            print signatures[sig] " " sig
        }
    }
' "$LOG_FILE" | sort -rn
"
    }
  ]
}
